podcast.title: Smartphone Music Video Production
podcast.body: Marcus Mumford adopted the trend of using smartphones, such as the iPhone 11, to create music videos in HD and 4K by the close of the 2010s. This highlights a shift towards more accessible and cost-effective production methods for professional-looking content. "people could create pro-level productions, especially after the debut of the iPhone 11. By the end of the decade, thousands of people were making music videos in HD and 4K with just their phones that included people like Lady Gaga and Selena Gomez and Marcus Mumford."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Precursor to Mumford & Sons (2007)
xref.body: This group, consisting of Marcus, Ted, and Winston, performed at the bar Communion, where Ben Lovett would occasionally join them on stage. By October 2007, they began recording together, which ultimately led to their transformation into Mumford & Sons. "Meanwhile, Marcus, Ted and Winston had coalesced in a group called Marcus Mumford and his Mary Men."

xref.title: Marcus Mumford's Crisis of Faith (2009)
xref.body: During the recording of *Sigh No More* in 2009, Marcus Mumford experienced a "crisis of faith," struggling to reconcile the allure of the "rock and roll world" with his parents' evangelical Christian beliefs. "And to make things even weirder, Marcus was having a crisis of faith."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Marcus Mumford's Career Path Change
xref.body: After attending Captain Kick and the Cowboy Ramblers' performance at The Bosens Locker, Marcus Mumford was so impressed that he dropped out of Edinburgh University, where he was expected to follow his parents into the ministry, and committed to music as his vocation. "Marcus was so impressed by what he heard and saw that he dropped out of university and vowed to make music his vocation."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Marcus Mumford's Family Background
xref.body: Marcus Mumford's English parents, John (a former "drug-taken hippie" turned ordained minister) and Eleanor (a proponent of faith healing), lived in Orange County, California, where they established a branch of the Vinyard Churches, a Christian evangelical organization, before moving back to London. "His English parents, John, a former drug-taken hippie turned ordained minister, and Eleanor, a proponent of faith healing, were living in Orange County, California at the time, right in the hearts of American punk rock country."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Marcus Mumford's Musical Influences
xref.body: Growing up, Marcus Mumford was exposed to Bob Dylan's music (especially his "God Love and Era" and the *O Brother, Where Art Thou?* soundtrack) and various jazz. He played in a jazz group as a teenager. "As he grew up, Marcus was exposed to the music of Bob Dylan, especially his God Love and Era, the old brother were at the O Soundtrack, and a variety of jazz."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Name Origin and Meaning
xref.body: The band evolved from "Marcus Mumford and his Mary Men" to "Mumford & Sons." This name choice, influenced by a trend of bands using "Sons" in their names, was appealing because it evoked the image of a traditional, family-owned general store or antique furniture shop. "So it came to pass that Mumford and his merry men became Mumford & Sons."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
